newsitem.title: FRANCE: Eurocourt rules against Britain in Saunders trial.
newsitem.headline: Eurocourt rules against Britain in Saunders trial.

text.p: The European Court of Human Rights ruled on Tuesday that Britain had denied a fair trial to Ernest Saunders, former chairman of the Guinness plc drinks group, who was convicted of fraud in 1990.

Saunders accused Britain of violating his right to a fair trial, saying evidence obtained from him by Department of Trade and Industry inspectors, who can legally oblige suspects to reply to questions or face fines or jail, was later used against him in a criminal prosecution.
The court also ordered the British government to pay Saunders, who was sacked as chairman of Guinness in 1987, 75,000 pounds ($124,500) in legal costs.
The ruling by 16 votes to four was an embarrassment for Britain, smarting from a string of recent court condemnations including for the killings of three Irish guerrillas in Gibraltar in 1988.

Saunders, now 61, was convicted in 1990 on 12 counts including false accounting and theft for inflating Guinness' share price to help its 1986 takeover of whisky group Distillers Plc prevail against rival bidder Argyll Plc.
